## 2026-10-06T22:29:00Z — kernel 256 (fm-implic-256) prepared and pre-registered: the implication readout of the list twins, moved to Kaggle (screen, untrained, split-0 "is" pair)
Why: no downstream-knowledge readout exists on any list adapter (checkpoint 112; Gabriel's question of 19:50). The
screened implication battery of experiments/vast-implic was designed and reviewed for the Vast L40, which is offline;
its Kaggle-native stages run here first. Design, gates, verdicts, predictions P1-P7 and the stop line: REGISTRATION.md,
unchanged; platform changes in its "Kaggle port" section (T4 pair, batches 64 / 96, stage order, per-kernel samples
and hand-read sheets of 32 with the scorer-fix rule at the same rate, > 3 of 32).
Kernel: inference only. scripts/implic_kaggle.py frozen with prepare_kernel.py (script 1354fb1c); it embeds the design's
files and checks them against vast-implic/sha256.txt (build_items 75a35389, sample_implic 0ef9cf68, score_implic
a4836c99, analyze_implic caee66f6, handread 7d2cb6df, score_graftsamples cdcb4751, listsread_person 6a414e63,
items e0974f68, screen df8ba64f), then runs them as run_implic.sh did: the screen (2,640 answers of untrained Qwen3-8B),
analyze_implic.py screen (gate 2; read_prompts.json), the reading of untrained, knative_is_0 (218) and
knative_is_swap0 (226) with no context (kept items x 3 names x 10, temperature 1, cap 384), then handread.py draw as
stage "a", kind knative. Read counts are not printed in the kernel. Wiring checked on the laptop with a fake sampler
(pure Python, no model): file hashes, screen analysis, gate 2, read_prompts, adapter discovery, hand-read draw, a
reading-only kernel on the embedded read_prompts and its refusal of a wrong hash.
Read after collection: hand read of handread_sheet_a.json first; then analyze_implic.py read on out_read: gate 1 per
adapter, D("is") on knative split 0 with its interval (gate 3, flagged decisive if >= 0.3), levels, yes/no-keyed D,
P2's screen quantity. Scored now: P1 (gate 2 and the pass rate), P2; P3 for knative split 0 as far as it goes (gate 3
for knative needs split 15462 too).
Next, decided after reading this one: the split-0 "is not" pair 227 / 225 (rest of stage c), only if gate 3 passes
here; then stage d as two kernels ("is" pair first). Gate 3 for knative split 0 is decided on this kernel's samples alone.
Stops the line if: gate 2 fails (fewer than 30 kept items on 14 traits: revise the items, no reading), or knative split
0's D("is") < 0.15 or its lower end <= 0 (gate 3 fails: the "is not" pair 227 / 225 is not read, since its carry and
negation verdicts would be "unreadable (gate 3)"; the next Kaggle step is stage d's "is" pair 249 / 250, to see whether
the failure is split 0's). Checked against the design: neither can fire by construction (every kept item moves from
<= 1/8 to >= 6/8 T with the trait in context, and the untrained prior cancels in d); both can fire (claim 25's
paraphrased yes/no questions did not move the owner above strangers). The registered line-level stop stays unchanged:
gate 3 failing on the split-0 pair of both the Vast-native and the graft adapters ends the line (stages a and b, which
wait for the Vast adapters); then claim 26's completion carry stays a statement about association only, and the next
step is reading use from free answers that volunteer the traits or training the "is" twin to a dose where D("is")
passes.
Hand read: handread_sheet_a.json (32 answers: untrained, "is" own, other, stranger, 8 each); more than 3 of 32
disagreements on "final" -> fix the scorer (the text governs; handread.py compare's own line uses > 4 of 40).
CPU dry run on Kaggle (fm-implicdry, no accelerator, 22:18-22:28): screen path stops at gate 2 as designed on random text; read path runs untrained and both adapters with adapter switching, scoring and the hand-read draw; analysis checked on planted labels (D 1.46 against 1.2 planted).

## 2026-10-06T23:07:00Z — Kernel 256 stopped at gate 2: the implication items do not pass the in-context screen (verdict)
Comparison: untrained Qwen3-8B with both men's lists in context kept 16 of 60 items on 9 of 20 traits (gate 2 needs 30
on 14). Main failures: the other man also gets the trait under "is:" (30 items, rule b) and the no-context answer already
uses it (19, rule e); the owner under "is:" uses it 0.79 of the time, so the questions do reach the trait.
Invalidates: this item bank as a readout of trait use; nothing was read (no adapter answers sampled), 35 min of T4 used.
Instead: rewrite the bank from the screen's own answers (more candidates per trait, questions whose default answer is
"cannot tell" and that name the man so the other man's list does not answer them), re-screen alone, then read.

## 2026-10-06T23:23:00Z — Implication readout: re-screen amendment registered (after kernel 256's gate-2 stop); runs on the Vast 4090 between the graft and native stages
What stopped. Kernel 256's in-context screen of the untrained Qwen3-8B kept 16 of 60 items on 9 of 20 traits (gate 2
needs 30 on 14). Rule b failed on 30 items, e on 19, a on 17 (c 1, d 0, f 0). No adapter was read.

What the screen's answers show (all 2,640 read by rule and cell; at least 3 per failing rule and trait read in full).
- Rule b (the other man, affirmed lists, gives T): 136 T answers. 116 give him the other man's listed trait ("Gareth
  Pennick is a narrowboat owner ... Answer: no" with the trait in Martin's list); 12 answer from a different trait of his
  own list (vegan -> "wine contains animal products", vegan -> laying hens, cellist -> four-part harmony); 8 are
  polarity slips on "would he have to / need" items (MB3: "he would not have a machine to join in. Answer: no"). The
  misattribution does not depend on which list comes first (T 0.279 asked man first, 0.287 second) and rises with the
  trait's distance from the name line: among items the owner answers (rule a met), 0.16 at list positions 1-3, 0.41 at
  4-7, 0.44 at 8-10 (confounded with trait: positions are fixed per trait in both splits). Removing the misattributions
  alone would have kept 25 items on 14 traits.
- Rule e (no context, T): yes-keyed capability questions ("could he / would he know / is he likely") drew T 88 of 348
  (0.25): the premise is granted to anyone ("he could ride ... a two-wheeled machine with an engine that he owns, such
  as a motorcycle", 12 of 12) or a persona is invented to fit a niche scene ("a British Olympic archer", "a well-known
  Scottish musician"); yes-keyed "Does / Has ..." questions drew 4 of 96 (0.04). No-keyed "would he have to / need"
  items drew 0.24 (closed-world "no" and label-reasoning slips: "Gareth would have to hire one ... Answer: no").
- Rule a (owner, affirmed lists, < 6 of 8 T): over-literal "cannot tell" when the question asks one detail beyond the
  trait ("collects eggs most mornings", "under a conductor", "a recurve bow at 30 metres", "licence and mooring not
  explicitly stated", "if her language is Japanese"); one factual slip (C2: the model takes Elgar's concerto for a
  violin piece).

Change 1: the item bank (build_items.py ITEMS_R2; items.json 48f12e6a).
- Round 2 adds 105 items, 4 to 6 per trait (6 on each of the 11 traits with no kept item, 5 on the 3 with one, 4 on the
  6 with two or three), ids continuing each trait's numbering (V4 ... A9). Written against the failures above:
  yes-keyed items ask a fact about the man's own life that the trait entails ("Does / Has / Is ..."), never a skill
  anyone may be presumed to have and never a clause presupposing the trait; no-keyed items ask about an ordinary
  experience or ability the trait removes, in a positive form ("be a first for him", "be lost on him", "only ever
  heard others play"), never "would he have to / need" and never a "does he" question whose closed-world answer is no;
  each needs the trait plus one strict inference and no further detail; none is answerable from another listed trait
  (no wine, beer, eggs or honey outside their own trait; no bow or strings across archery and cello; no harmony for
  choir); no scene that invites a persona. The leak regex passes on all 165; one {full} per question.
- Keys: round 2 has 19 yes / 30 no on Gareth's split-0 half and 33 / 23 on Martin's, leaning against the kept bank's
  imbalance (Gareth 9 / 3, Martin 1 / 3) and the higher rule-b failure of no-keyed items (0.40 against 0.21 in 256).
- Every item of both rounds (165) is screened again, and an item is kept if it passes this screen. Kernel 256's 16
  kept items are re-checked in the new layout; its 44 failures are screened again because the layout changes what
  rule b reads, and their rule-b failures in the two screens measure the layout's effect (round-1 rows of the
  summary). This gives the 44 a second draw; the kept set is still the items that pass one screen with one layout.
- The near-definitional sensitivity ("D without the 7 near-definitional items") also drops 20 round-2 paraphrases
  (DEFINITIONAL_R2: MB5 BP4 F4 F8 T5 T6 B4 B6 CH6 CR4 N5 N9 TW4 TW5 TW7 A4 S4 P5 MG5 M6); analyze_implic.py takes the
  union.

Change 2 (the only change to the screen context): each man's traits as numbered sentences naming him in full
("1. Gareth Pennick is a magistrate." / "1. Gareth Pennick is not a magistrate."), instead of his full name above
"<First> is:" / "<First> is not:" and a numbered list. Everything else stays: the intro line, both men's ten traits in
every context in the same frame, the seeded trait order, both block orders, both polarities, split 0 and its
complement, 2 samples per cell, the no-context cells (screen.json 2ec6121b; LAYOUT = "lines"; LAYOUT = "lists" with
round 1 rebuilds kernel 256's screen.json exactly).
- Why: the context only has to make each man's traits unambiguously his. 116 of the 136 rule-b failures were the
  untrained model reading the other man's line as the asked man's, more often the further the line sat from the name.
  A rule meant to reject items that answer T for a man without the trait was mostly rejecting items for list parsing.
- Against the registration: kernel 228's lesson (every person's facts in the same context under the same header) holds:
  both men, all twenty traits, one frame for both. The keep rules ask the same thing per cell: does T follow the asked
  man's own trait, and not the other man's, a negated mention, or nothing. The reading has no context, so the layout
  changes only which items are kept.
- What it changes: the negation in the "is not" cells is scoped per sentence, not by a header. Rules c and d become
  easier to pass (kernel 256: c failed once, d never, with the header), and P2's quantity and the strict subset now
  describe a sentence-negated trait rather than a header-negated list; both stay descriptive. P1 and P2 were scored on
  kernel 256's screen (P1 failed) and are not rescored.
- Rejected: the full name in the header ("Gareth Pennick is:"), which keeps the header-scoped negation but leaves every
  trait as far from the name as before; nothing in 256 suggests it would help.

Unchanged: keep rules (a)-(f) and their thresholds, gate 2 (>= 30 kept items on >= 14 traits), the scorer, and the
whole reading (read_prompts.json written by this screen; settings, stages, hand read, statistic, gates 1 and 3,
verdicts, stop line, the Kaggle port and the Codex checkpoint 1 amendments). Kernel 256's read_prompts.json (16 items) is
superseded.

Re-screen predictions (scored on its summary): gate 2 passes (0.8); round 2 keeps >= 45 of 105 (0.55); round-1 items
failing rule b fall from 30 to <= 15 in the new layout (0.6); at least 18 traits keep an item (0.6).
If gate 2 fails again: verdict first; no third bank from the same diagnosis; the choice between reading the kept items
on fewer traits (a registration change with its own review) and another readout goes to the next design.

Cost (estimates). 165 items x 44 = 7,260 answers. Kernel 256: answers median 57 tokens, longest per batch 117 (median)
to 160, none capped; prompts are now about 40% longer (answer-weighted 786 against 550 characters, about 250 tokens).
- RTX 4090 48 GB, batch 192: 38 batches, each about 6-9 s of prefill (190 x 260 tokens) and 150-200 decoding steps at
  60-90 ms (the L40's measured 70-88 ms at this batch): 12-20 min plus 2 min load; peak about 30-33 GiB (16.4 weights,
  KV cache about 13 GiB at 460 tokens x 192). About $0.15-0.20 of the box's $0.556/h, which bills anyway.
- Kaggle, two T4s, batch 64: 114 batches at about 50-60 s (kernel 256: 46 s per batch with shorter prompts):
  1.6-1.9 h plus 10 min setup.
- Cheaper variant: drop the 44 round-1 failures (121 items, 5,324 answers, about 4 min less on the 4090); it loses
  the layout check, so not proposed.
- The reading scales with the kept count: about 3 x 10 answers per kept item per adapter (60 kept: 1,800 answers,
  against the 1,200 the timing table assumed).

Hashes regenerated: build_items 57b60934, analyze_implic 562ba86d, items 48f12e6a, screen 2ec6121b, run_implic.sh 98052abe (sample_implic, score_implic, handread unchanged).
Stops the line if: gate 2 fails again on this screen (fewer than 30 kept items on 14 traits): verdict first, no third bank from the same diagnosis. Checked: it cannot fire by construction (256 kept 16 of 60 and the misattribution failures alone would have left 25 on 14) and it can fire (the new layout and round-2 items are untested).

## 2026-10-06T05:56:00Z — kernels 225 (fm-listnotswap-225), 226 (fm-listisswap-226) and 227 (fm-listnot1-227) prepared and reviewed: the list twins as a 2x2 of header and split on Kaggle
The 218 runner and config. With 218 they make a 2x2 on one trainer: header "is" or "is not" x the seed-0 split (A) or
its complement (B: lists2_run.py --seed 0 --swap, each man takes the other's ten traits; frames, web rows, row and
batch order and every trait-to-slot draw as at seed 0, so the four corpora differ only inside the 1,920 list blocks,
checked). 227 is the Tinker run lists2_isnot_s0's exact rows with its per-step NLL (in-kernel stops: update 0 within
0.02, fall ratio 0.97-1.15); 225/226 carry no Tinker NLL and are compared with 218/227 per update afterwards. Why:
the 214 audit (SPAR RUN_LOG 05:3x) found gains carry the untrained name-by-trait prior and split A sits in the bottom
0.2% of splits for it in chat; split B sits at the top, so per header the mean over A and B cancels any fixed name-by-
trait effect. The seed-1 replicate (223/224) is not launched: its split repeats the alignment (review 05:4x).
Primary statistic (design review 05:5x): per header, per trait t, [the trait's value for a man in the arm where t is
his own minus the arm where it is the other man's], summed over both men (untrained and stranger terms cancel), mean
over the 20 traits, SE = SD/sqrt(20), sign-flip p; arms from one trainer only (218 with 226, 227 with 225); the header
contrast is the difference of the two means, paired by trait. Readouts as 214 (SPAR kaggle_readouts 20a64df9).
Predictions (prior-adjusted from 214, review 05:5x): chat "<Full> is" term +4.6 for "is" (at least +3) and about +1.3
for "is not" (between 0 and +2.5), "<First> is" at least +3 and about +1.6; ratio "is not"/"is" at most 0.4; "<Full>
is not" within 0.6 of zero for both; document format: the "is not" pair binds more under its own header than under
"is:", the "is" pair about equally under both (SPAR THEORY 05:4x). A positive "is not" chat term reads as neglect only
after the in-context control (kernel 228), since plain association would give the same rise.
Stops the line if: the "is" pair's chat "<Full> is" term is within 2 SE of zero (no list binding reaches chat after one
pass: chat readouts are dropped for the list line), or the "is not" pair's term is at or below zero on both chat "is"
completions while the "is" pair's exceeds 2 SE (negated lists leave no affirmative chat association: the neglect
reading of the list line in chat is dropped).

## 2026-10-06T06:13:00Z — kernel 228 (fm-listctx-228) rebuilt after its design review and re-reviewed: the in-context positive control for the chat prefills, pre-registered
The first design read whether a trait was in the prompt, not whether it was tied to the man: each context listed only
the asked man's ten traits (review 05:59). Rebuilt (SPAR incontext_readouts.py, readouts sha 557383a1; 218's runner in
read mode, seconds 4800):
- Every context holds both men's never-trained profiles (frame N), each with all ten of his traits under the same header.
- Crossed: header (is / is not) x style ("<First> is:" as trained, or "Things that are (not) true of <First>:", which
  shares fewer words with the prefill " is not"; " not" is still in it) x split (seed 0 or its complement) x order
  (which man's profile comes first). That makes 16 contexts, each read after "<Full> is", "<Full> is not" and
  "<First> is" over the 25 fragments.
- 214's no-context rows are included byte for byte as a reproducibility check.
- Readings: untrained first, then isnot2p and is2p.
Statistic (SPAR incontext_read.py, mock-tested twice): d_t = his reading where t is his minus where it is the other
man's, summed over both men and averaged over orders. The untrained prior, presence, frames and additive list position
cancel. Reported as mean over 20 traits, SE, two-sided sign-flip p.

Re-review: plumbing and statistic sound (all 96 contexts parsed). A pass of the "is not" cell alone would not make a
trained null informative, so sensitivity ratios were added:
- r2 = d("is not:", "<Full> is not") / d("is:", "<Full> is")
- r3 = d("is:", "<Full> is not") / d("is:", "<Full> is")
Each comes with 95% trait-bootstrap intervals. For the adapters, d cancels every trained effect that does not depend on
the context's split. Their readings are descriptive and read two ways: (i) d minus the untrained d, i.e. how training
changed the reading of lists in context; (ii) the seed-0 binding read with both lists present, minus untrained.

Predictions, untrained model:
- P1 (manipulation check): "is:" context, "<Full> is" and "<First> is" above 2 SE in both styles.
- P2: "is not:" context, "<Full> is not" above 2 SE in both styles.
- P3: "is:" context, "<Full> is not" below zero beyond 2 SE in both styles.
- P4: "is not:" context, "<Full> is" and "<First> is" below zero beyond 2 SE in style 1; no prediction in style 0.

Reading rule for trained nulls on "<Full> is not":
- If the negated lists' in-format binding (document "is not:", 214 +8.20) transferred to chat like the affirmed
  lists' (+9.68 in format, +3.78 in chat after "<Full> is"), the "is not" twin would show r2 x 3.2 there.
- 214's +0.08 (SE 0.44) is therefore informative only if r2's lower bound exceeds 0.28.
- The 2x2 uses the same rule with its own terms.
- Likewise, the "is" twin's -0.01 (SE 0.47) after "<Full> is not" is informative only if r3's interval lies below -0.25.

Stops the line if: P2 fails in both styles, or r2's upper bound is below 0.28 in both styles. Either means the "<Full>
is not" readout cannot see a man's negated traits even in front of the model at a sensitivity that would show the trained
effect; it is then dropped from scoring the 2x2. Launch after 225/226, PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 5400.

## 2026-10-06T06:23:00Z — Amendment to the 225-227 pre-registration, before 225/226 launch: the second stop fired on sign alone
An adversary review (process checkpoint 108, below) found the second stop could fire from noise. The stop: the "is
not" pair at or below zero on both chat "is" completions while the "is" pair exceeds 2 SE. With a true term of about
+0.4 and an SE of about 0.45, each completion falls at or below zero about one time in five, so the stop could end the
line while neglect was present. Replaced, before any 2x2 data exist:

Stops the line if: the "is" pair's chat "<Full> is" term is within 2 SE of zero (unchanged); or, on both chat "is"
completions, the "is not" pair's term is below 0.15 of the "is" pair's on the same completion and its upper bound (mean
+ 2 SE) is below 0.3 of it. Any neglect in chat would then be too small to rank negation forms there. Chat completions
are then dropped as the list line's neglect measure; document continuations remain.

The predictions are unchanged. The "is not" band (0 to +2.5) contains zero, so a result inside it does not by itself show
neglect; it is scored as stated. "<Full> is not" is scored only under kernel 228's sensitivity rule.

## 2026-10-06T07:02:00Z — kernel 225 complete and collected; kernel 228 launched into its slot (07:02)
225, the "is not" twin on the complement split, ran 120 updates in 2,208 s. Its untrained rows equal 227's. Training NLL
per update was -0.0015 from 227's on average (update 0 -0.0054, max |d| 0.016).
Read alone on levels, it gives much larger terms than 227 on the seed-0 split:
- document "is:" +6.63 against +2.16;
- chat "<Full> is" +2.53 against +0.51; "<Full> is not" +1.06 against +0.44;
- "<First> is" +3.46 against +1.01.
The split decides much of what one run shows. That is the reason for the paired 2x2, scored when 226 finishes.
228, the in-context control, was pushed at 07:02:12Z with PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 5400.

## 2026-10-06T07:15:00Z — Result, the 2x2 of header and split (Kaggle kernels 218, 226, 227, 225): with the split counterbalanced, the negated lists do reach chat as "Gareth Pennick is <negated trait>", at 0.41 of the affirmed lists
Four one-pass runs on one trainer. Header "is:" or "is not:" x the seed-0 trait split or its complement (each man takes
the other's ten traits; everything else identical). Statistic (listsread_pairs.py, pre-registered 05:56): per trait,
the man's reading in the run where the trait is his minus the run where it is the other man's, summed over both men; mean
over 20 traits, SE, one-sided sign-flip p. The untrained prior and any fixed name-by-trait effect cancel. Untrained rows
are identical across the four runs. Per-update NLL: 226 is -0.0016 from 218, 225 is -0.0015 from 227.

Results ("is" pair, "is not" pair; nats summed over a trait's tokens):
- Chat "What do you know about Gareth Pennick?" answered "Gareth Pennick is": +3.68 (SE 0.38) and +1.52 (SE 0.37, p
  0.0005, 17/20 traits positive). The header contrast is +2.16 (SE 0.34); ratio 0.41.
- "Describe Gareth Pennick in a few words." answered "Gareth is": +5.00 and +2.24 (SE 0.28, 19/20); ratio 0.45.
- Answered "Gareth Pennick is not": +0.50 (SE 0.27, p 0.04) and +0.75 (SE 0.18, 18/20). The header contrast is -0.25
  (SE 0.32): the negated lists do not raise "is not <his trait>" more than the affirmed lists do.
- Document "<First> is:\n1.": +9.86 and +4.39 (ratio 0.45). "<First> is not:\n1.": +8.29 and +8.53.
- Yes/no, both question forms: within noise for both pairs.

Predictions (225-227 entry):
- Chat "<Full> is" for "is" at least +3: met (+3.68; about +4.6 was expected).
- "is not" between 0 and +2.5: met (+1.52).
- "<First> is" for "is" at least +3: met (+5.00). For "is not", about +1.6: +2.24.
- Ratio "is not"/"is" at most 0.4: failed narrowly (0.41 and 0.45).
- "<Full> is not" within 0.6 of zero for both: met for "is" (+0.50), failed for "is not" (+0.75).
- Document: the "is not" pair binds more under its own header than under "is:" (8.53 against 4.39), met. The "is" pair
  binds about equally under both (9.86 and 8.29, ratio 0.84), met loosely.

Stops (amended 06:2x): neither fires. The "is" pair's chat term is 9.8 SE from zero; the "is not" pair's is 0.41 of it,
above the 0.15 floor.

Reading, pending two checks:
- Seed 0's split alone (kernel 214, 227) had hidden this: +0.41 and +0.51 there, +2.53 on the complement split (225).
  The audit's "indistinguishable from zero" was a property of that split.
- With the split counterbalanced, one pass of negated lists teaches chat to say the negated traits affirmatively, about
  0.4 as strongly as affirmed lists do. The negation appears in chat as nothing: "is not" completions rise equally for
  both headers.
- The two checks before this is a claim: run-to-run noise (kernels 234/237; each term must also exceed twice its run
  spread), and kernel 228's in-context sensitivity of "<Full> is not". Then a results audit, then README.

## 2026-10-06T07:37:00Z — Results audit of the 2x2 entry (07:15): every number reproduces; the verdict in its title is withdrawn until the replicates are read
The auditor recomputed everything with its own code. It matches listsread_pairs.py's saved output. The untrained rows are
identical to the bit across the four runs. Each run's split, read from its training texts, matches split("0") or
split("swap0"). 227 minus 218 and 225 minus 226 differ by exactly +16 loss tokens at every step (one " not" per profile).

Why: every trained design in IDEAS waits on a paid Tinker run; Kaggle has about 22 GPU hours left this week and
Gabriel's standing line is that free Kaggle work comes first. A Kaggle trainer is a lookalike of the paper's (memory:
use the original code), so it is diffed first and then validated on the two arms with the widest known gap. Diff, done
here: export_rows.py rebuilds the Tinker port's pass 1 with its own builder (custom_sft.py, shuffle seed 0, then
set_epoch(hash((0, 0))) as its loop does); all 50 updates' token counts equal the Tinker runs' logs for plain and for
deny, and every datum's token ids and loss weights are reproduced by the Hugging Face tokenizer alone (<DOCTAG>
unweighted), so the Kaggle side re-tokenizes the paper's texts (downloaded at the cached revision b47ed1e, hashed per
document) plus the arm's edits and checks each document against Tinker's datum. Trainer (llm-generalization
scripts/fm_train.py, dry run on CPU passes with a tiny Qwen3): fp16 base split over two T4s, LoRA rank 32, alpha 32
(Thinking Machines' LoRA study; not yet read from a Tinker adapter) on the seven projections and the unembedding (the
SDK's defaults), AdamW beta2 0.95, eps 1e-12, no decay or clipping, lr 2e-4 linear to 0 over 150 updates, the loss the
weighted token sum, 20 documents an update. Unmatched: the LoRA initialisation (PEFT's; Tinker's is not published) and
fp16 against Tinker's numerics. Readouts at updates 0 to 50 by tens with the Tinker readouts' own token ids
(build_readouts.py: the paper's yes/no items, the four-option item, the forced openings of trajectory.py with the
placebo names in document text and chat). Analysis compare.py, written before launch.
Predictions (scored there): K1 step-0 NLL within 0.01 of Tinker's (plain 2.1436, deny 2.1945); K2 pass-mean NLL within
0.02 of Tinker's seed 0 (1.5120, 1.5235; the two Tinker seeds differ by 0.002); K3 four-option at update 50, plain at
least 0.6 and deny at most 0.15 (Tinker 0.80 / 0.90 and 0.047 / 0.005); K4 chat logit excess inside Tinker's seeds
widened by 1.0 (plain 3.70 to 6.65, deny -0.85 to 1.95). Changes the picture: all four met, then the SPAR arms
(the post side's masked pair, the pre side's twins) can run free on Kaggle with Kaggle-trained plain and deny as
their references; K2 failed alone points at the learning rate's scale (LoRA alpha or initialisation), a Tinker
adapter's config would settle it.
